steps.body: Write how many: count the group carefully, and the numeral you write is the last number you said. Counting and writing join hands.
steps.narration: Write how many: count the group carefully, and the numeral you write is the last number you said. Counting and writing join hands.

widget.prompt: Count the group of 9, then show the amount your numeral must record.

commonCounts.feedback: The count did not stop at eight; one more dot carried it to nine.
Ten overshoots the count; the numeral copies the last word said, nine.

widget.missFeedback: Count to the end first; the final word is the mark to write.
widget.successFeedback: Nine — the count ended there, so the written mark must say 9.

predict.prompt: You count 1 to 9. Which numeral do you write?
predict.reveal: The written numeral records where the count FINISHED, not where it began.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write count.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write count.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: Kai counts her blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. How many blocks does she have?

options.feedback: Correct — the last number said, 6, is the one the numeral must record.
The count stopped at 6; writing one more would record a block that is not there.
That records one too few — the count reached 6, so the numeral must too.
That runs two past the count; the written numeral copies the last word said, 6.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 11? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 10.
9 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 11 to reach 10.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 11: you land on 10.
widget.successFeedback: 10 — the numeral written just before 11 names one less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 11 reaches 10.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 11 means a single hop back, stopping on 10.
